Family essay and a conversation with the author's mother. Three personal forward-looking remarks about the children; the mother's remarks are not the author's.
RAMHT SF 2026 event promotion with a news roundup. Event date and speaker roster logged; news bullets are past or present-tense reports.

statements.quote: You can even comment guessing who you think the company is, and I'm never gonna confirm or deny the answer.
statements.context: Introduction to a post recounting a peer-to-peer review call with an unnamed reviewer at a redacted insurance company. The author keeps the insurer's identity secret and states he will never confirm or deny reader guesses about which company it is.
statements.note: Trivial statement of the author's own future conduct in a playful frame; low forecast value.

statements.quote: Our investigation of this particular course of action suggests that you will get faster attention within the insurance company, because these formal complaints directly to an insurance company require reporting to their regulator and to their accreditation body.
statements.context: Part Four of the Q&A. Joe Feldman (Cover My Mental Health) advises clinicians facing a denial to file a formal insurer complaint and predicts that this gets faster attention because the complaint must be reported to the regulator and accreditation body. The author asks the questions and does not restate the claim.
statements.note: Third-party generic conditional prediction (Feldman); logged for recall, not adopted by the author in his own words.

statements.quote: I have another live event coming up, Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment, a.k.a. RAMHT 2026 APA . It's happening on May 16th, in San Francisco, and you can get your tickets now.
statements.context: Opening paragraph of a post recommending the Drug Story podcast. The author announces his own live event RAMHT 2026 APA (co-created with Grady Hannah) for May 16, 2026 in San Francisco.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate. Restated in posts 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 of this packet.

statements.quote: Neurolief raises another $6M from lead investor BrainsWay to bring ProlivRx to market.
statements.context: Bullet in a list of 'recent media hits' at the end of the post. Neurolief (the author is its Chief Medical Officer) raised $6M from BrainsWay; the stated purpose is to bring the ProlivRx at-home neuromodulation device to market.
statements.note: Purpose clause in a news bullet, not an explicit prediction; own organization (CONTROL candidate).

statements.quote: have joined the club as sponsors (among others to be announced!) of our next events
statements.context: Closing paragraph about RAMHT, 'the live-action version of this newsletter'. The author lists Salma Health, Beckley Clinical, NRx, Graymatters Health, Ampa Health, Simple Practice, Emobot, Psyrin, Videra Health and Definium Therapeutics as sponsors of the next RAMHT events and says more sponsors will be announced.
statements.note: Own-event sponsorship claim plus a promise of further sponsor announcements; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: We will be bringing more tools for advocacy to the masses!
statements.context: Final sentence of the RAMHT sponsor paragraph. The author promises that RAMHT/the newsletter will bring more advocacy tools to a broad audience.
statements.note: Vague own-activity promise; low forecast value.

statements.quote: I had a blast working with Rob on this article, and there's more to come from us
statements.context: After excerpting a Healio article on ketamine and AMPA receptor PET imaging co-written with Rob Glatter, M.D., the author says more co-authored work from the two of them is coming.
statements.note: Own-activity promise; low forecast value.

statements.quote: Dear readers, I am trying to get Trent to chime in also. It is likely to take your urging as well.
statements.context: Introduction to an interview with the author's daughter Quinn on her 10th birthday. The author wants his son Trent to appear in the newsletter too and predicts it will take readers' urging to make that happen.
statements.note: Personal/family item; hedged; low forecast value.

statements.quote: I am very aware this is not going to be the kind of birthday they want much longer.
statements.context: Opening of a family essay. The author's twins chose to spend their 10th birthday with their parents instead of a party with friends; he predicts they will not want that kind of birthday for much longer.
statements.note: Personal/family prediction; not resolvable from public sources.

statements.quote: This excuse is going to run out quickly.
statements.context: The author's son Trent declines to use a knife for dinner prep, saying 'Come on, Dad, I'm not even 10!' The author predicts this excuse will stop working soon because Trent has just turned 10.
statements.note: Personal/family remark; trivial.

statements.quote: He said it with the kind of reserved confidence that will do well in senior management.
statements.context: Trent reads an upsetting email sent to his mother Carlene and calmly says the sender seems unhappy. The author characterizes his son's reserved confidence as the kind that will do well in senior management.
statements.note: Borderline: a characterization of a trait rather than a prediction about a future state; logged with forward_looking false for the coder to judge.

statements.quote: On May 16, 2026, on the first night of the American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting, we return to San Francisco to have rapid conversations about rapid-acting treatments and assessments.
statements.context: Promotional post for RAMHT (Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment), 'a Grady Hannah and The Frontier Psychiatrists production'. The author states the event returns to San Francisco on May 16, 2026, the first night of the APA Annual Meeting.
statements.note: Own-event date announcement; CONTROL candidate; restates the May 16 date given in post 2.

statements.quote: So, who will be there, you ask? Carlene MacMillan, MD, FCTMSS, DFAACAP Chief Product Officer, Radial
statements.context: Speaker roster for RAMHT SF 2026 (May 16, 2026). The quote captures the head of the list; the full roster names Carlene MacMillan (Radial), Owen Muir (Radial and Neurolief), Colleen Hanlon (BrainsWay), Zeena Ojjeh (Salma Health), Kirk Thelander (Graymatters Health), Jacob Donoghue (Beacon Biosignals), Jonathan Javitt (NRx), Dominik Middelmann (MDHub), Grady Hannah (NightWare/RAMHT), Dan Karlin (Definium), Josh Stevens and Jordan Sloshower (Beckley Clinical), Chris Dougherty (Hydra Strategies), Sofia Matta (Harvard/MGH) and Joe Feldman (Cover My Mental Health).
statements.note: Forward-looking attendance/speaker claim for the author's own event; the horizon comes from the event date stated earlier in the post. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: In that future, we'll have brains that don't break down on their owners as often, and when they do, we fix them promptly.
statements.context: Opening of a manifesto for 'Brain Medicine'. The newsletter 'advocates for a better future'; the author describes that future as one where brains break down less often and are fixed promptly, likening brain care to plumbing.
statements.note: Aspirational vision statement without a date; borderline between advocacy and forecast.

statements.quote: This is gonna take a change in public consciousness. We're gonna stop talking about mental health—Mental health is just a subdomain of Brain Medicine.
statements.context: The author argues that Brain Medicine should be a single plumbing-like discipline and predicts that the field will stop using the term 'mental health', which he calls a subdomain of Brain Medicine.
statements.note: Compound: a precondition (change in public consciousness) plus a prediction that 'mental health' as a term is abandoned. No date.

statements.quote: Brain Medicine is our future terminal specialty that brings together the existing disciplines of psychology, psychiatry, neurology, neuroradiology, and neurosurgery, with all working together under one overarching umbrella.
statements.context: Core claim of the Brain Medicine manifesto: a future unified specialty combining psychology, psychiatry, neurology, neuroradiology and neurosurgery under one umbrella, so that 'if your brain doesn't work, you call a brain medicine doctor'.
statements.note: Vision statement asserting a future unified specialty; no date.

statements.quote: it wasn't obvious to us—yet—that "mental health" as a term was approaching the end of its lifespan, like the USB-A cable of its day.
statements.context: Reflecting on co-creating RAMHT with Grady Hannah, the author says the term 'mental health' is approaching the end of its lifespan, comparing it to the USB-A cable.
statements.confidence_phrase: approaching the end of its lifespan
statements.note: Trend call that the term 'mental health' will fall out of use; restates the 'stop talking about mental health' claim earlier in the post.

statements.quote: It is a live event, we've done it 5 times now, with 6 and 7 coming up!
statements.context: About RAMHT, the live event co-created with Grady Hannah: five editions done, editions 6 and 7 coming up. The following call to action gives RAMHT SF 2026 on May 16 as the next one.
statements.note: Own-event plan: two more RAMHT editions; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Then, Optum announced it would expand TMS coverage, allowing nurse practitioners in independent practice states to prescribe the first safe and effective treatment for brain disorders under this new brain medicine paradigm.
statements.context: Press roundup for Radial. The author reports that Optum announced an expansion of TMS coverage allowing nurse practitioners in independent-practice states to prescribe TMS, and that he was quoted on it in Behavioral Health Business.
statements.note: Reported payer announcement (Optum's stated future action), not the author's own forecast; logged for recall.

statements.quote: Another recent Healio article noted that neuromodulation is coming to the home!
statements.context: The author cites a Healio article on the FDA approval (PMA P250010) of Neurolief's Proliv Rx home-use system for MDD and endorses its claim that neuromodulation is coming to the home.
statements.note: Endorsed restatement of a Healio trend claim; the example device belongs to the author's own company Neurolief (CONTROL candidate).

statements.quote: Next, I have to get to a meeting with our friends at Compass Pathways to talk about how we're going to get psychedelic medicines like COMP360 to the world.
statements.context: The author (Radial CMO) mentions a meeting with Compass Pathways, Radial's collaboration partner, about how they will get psychedelic medicines such as COMP360 (psilocybin) to the world.
statements.note: Implicit expectation that COMP360 reaches patients via the Radial-Compass collaboration; own organization (CONTROL candidate). Not an explicit approval call.

statements.quote: Through the grant program, Compass expects to award up to three organizations grants to support the development of foundational psychedelic and COMP360-specific training. Applications will be accepted from April 14 through May 14, 2026.
statements.context: Quoted Compass Pathways announcement (April 14, 2026) of a training grant program: up to three organizations to receive grants for psychedelic and COMP360-specific training, applications open April 14 to May 14, 2026.
statements.note: Quoted third-party press release; the author does not adopt it in his own words.

statements.quote: As we prepare for the potential commercial launch of COMP360 for treatment-resistant depression, our priority is ensuring that healthcare providers are trained, confident, and ready to deliver COMP360 treatment responsibly where eligible patients may receive care ... ready to deliver psilocybin treatment at scale, if approved.
statements.context: Quoted statement by Dr. Steve Levine, Chief Patient Officer at Compass Pathways, in the training-grant announcement: Compass is preparing for a potential commercial launch of COMP360 for treatment-resistant depression and wants providers ready to deliver psilocybin treatment at scale if approved.
statements.note: Quoted third party; hedged launch/approval expectation ('potential', 'if approved'); the author reproduces it without explicit endorsement.

statements.quote: It's not huge yet
statements.context: Public-health update on cephalosporin non-susceptible ('super') gonorrhea in New York City. After asking 'How big a problem is this?', the author says it is not huge yet, then quotes NYC data: 0.4% of 2025 isolates showed reduced susceptibility to ceftriaxone or cefixime.
entities: New York State Department of Health
statements.note: Borderline: implicit expectation via 'yet' that non-susceptible gonorrhea will grow beyond 0.4% of NYC isolates. Public health, outside the ledger's core areas.

statements.note: Ad-block restatement of the RAMHT SF 2026 date first given in post 2; CONTROL candidate.
